speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started and if you experienced any trauma to the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear or feel a "pop" at the moment of injury, and are you currently able to fully straighten the tip of your finger? I need to assess for a potential mallet finger or tendon injury.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your description of the finger being stuck in an extended position and the inability to flex the distal joint, I suspect a volar plate injury or a dislocation. Can you confirm if the fingertip is angled downward (flexed) compared to the other fingers, and does the pain worsen when you try to straighten it?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Right_ring_finger_X-ray
I need to rule out a fracture or dislocation given the mechanism of injury and the finger's extended resting position.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the X-ray is negative for fractures or dislocations, the inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint suggests a rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon, often called a "jersey finger." Can you confirm if you feel a gap or retraction in the tendon just below the fingertip when you try to make a fist?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the mechanism of injury and the inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint despite a normal X-ray, this is highly suggestive of a flexor digitorum profundus avulsion, commonly known as "jersey finger."

DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey finger (Flexor digitorum profundus rupture)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
